title: Hazardous Materials & Battery Handling Protocol
content:
1. Battery Storage: All lead-acid and lithium forklift batteries must be charged only in designated Charging Station Alpha (Bay 15). Proper eye protection and rubber gloves are mandatory.

2. Acid Spill Protocol: In the event of battery electrolyte leakage, immediately alert the Floor Supervisor. Deploy the Acid Neutralizing Spill Kit located at Pillar 14. Do not flush chemical spills down the drain.

3. Ventilation: The charging bay exhaust fans must run continuously 24/7 to prevent hydrogen gas buildup.

title: Pallet Stacking & Racking Regulations
content:
1. Stacking Limits: In Zone A (Heavy Goods), pallets may be stacked up to a maximum of 3 tiers high. In Zone C (High Turnover), double stacking (maximum 2 tiers) is the absolute limit for safety.

2. Damaged Pallets: Any wooden pallet with cracked stringers or missing boards must be tagged with a RED TAG and transferred to the Quarantine Staging Area at Bay 9.

3. Overhang Rules: Product overhang must not exceed 2 inches on any side of standard 48x40 inch GMA pallets.

title: Forklift & Mobile Equipment Safety Protocol
content:
1. Speed Limits: Maximum speed for forklifts and reach trucks inside warehouse aisles is 5 mph (8 km/h). Speed in the main cross-dock corridor is strictly capped at 8 mph.

2. Pedestrian Right-of-Way: Pedestrians wearing high-visibility vests always have unconditional right-of-way. Operators must sound horn at all blind intersections and aisle exits.

3. High-Value Secure Cages: High-value electronics (Category E) must be stored in the Secure Cage inside Zone B. Access requires keycard authorization from a Shift Supervisor.

title: Customer Returns & Reverse Logistics SOP Documentation
content:
1. RMA Verification: All inbound returns must be verified against an active Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA) number before unloading at Receiving Dock 3.

2. Inspection & Grading: Grade A items (unopened box, undamaged seals) are returned to active stock in Zone B. Grade B items (opened box, complete accessories) are directed to the repackaging line.

3. Quarantine & Scrap: Any returned item showing physical defects, water damage, or electrical fault must be tagged and transferred to the Returns Quarantine Area at Bay 11.

title: Inventory quantities and stock question guide
content:
Stock quantity definitions: On-hand is the recorded total quantity. Reserved is committed stock. Quarantined stock is unavailable for picking. Available stock excludes reserved and quarantined balances. Unassigned stock has a recorded balance but lacks a verified bin assignment. Use current inventory database results for quantities; this guide does not contain current product balances.

Inventory question examples: Which products have equal number of units? Which products have the same available quantity? Which product has the highest stock? List products with more than 100 units. Show products with exactly 0 units. Show products with at least 10 available units. Inventory comparisons read the current authoritative PostgreSQL snapshot and include a data timestamp. Equal quantity comparisons group products with the same stored unit of measure and include zero quantities. A result with no matches is a valid answer.

Product lookup examples: Search by SKU, stable product ID, name or alias. Ask where a product is stored to retrieve all recorded bins, warehouses and floors. Warehouse-scoped questions use assigned bin balances only; unassigned stock is not assigned to a guessed warehouse. Missing placements or history must be reported as missing. Company procedures require actual approved documents; general guidance is not a substitute for those documents.
